ex.en: My brother-in-law passed away last Wednesday.
ex.ja: 先週の水曜日、義理の兄が亡くなりました。

ex.en: I work every other day: Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
ex.ja: 月曜、水曜、金曜と私は１日おきに働いている。

ex.en: Our club will hold its monthly meeting next Wednesday.
ex.ja: 私たちのクラブは次の水曜日に月例会を開きます。

note.ja: 古英語 Wōdnesdæg（主神オーディンの日）。ラテン語 dies Mercurii（メルクリウスの日）を置き換えた。

en: To allow to enter; to grant entrance (to), whether into a place, into the mind, or into consideration.
To allow (someone) to enter a profession or to enjoy a privilege; to recognize as qualified for a franchise.

admit.ety: From Middle English admitten, amitten, borrowed from Old French admettre, amettre (“to admit”), from Latin admittō (“to allow entrance, inlet”, literally “to send to”), from ad- + mittere (“to send”).

ex.en: The man admitted having broken into the house.
ex.ja: 男はその家に押し入ったことを認めた。

ex.en: Three Chinese students were admitted to the college.
ex.ja: ３人の中国人留学生がその大学に入学が許された。

ex.en: Children under three are admitted free of charge.
ex.ja: 三歳未満の子供は入場無料です。

note.ja: ad（〜へ）+ mit（送る）。中へ送り入れる →「入ることを許す・認める」。

en: The position of the body or way of carrying oneself.
A disposition or state of mind.
To assume or to place in a particular position or orientation; to pose.
To express an attitude through one's posture, bearing, tone of voice, etc.

attitude.ety: From French attitude, from Italian attitudine (“attitude, aptness”), from Medieval Latin aptitūdō (“aptitude”) and actitūdō (“acting, posture”), from Latin aptō and actitō. Doublet of aptitude.

ex.en: Try to have a positive attitude about everything.
ex.ja: 何事にも積極的な態度を取るようにしなさい。

ex.en: The attitude holds good in such a situation.
ex.ja: その態度はその状況においては有効だ。

ex.en: I don't have a problem with his attitude.
ex.ja: 彼の態度に問題はない。

note.ja: イタリア語 attitudine（姿勢）から。ラテン語 aptitudo（適性）。aptitude と同じ語源。「体の構え」→「心の構え」。

en: The woody part of a tree arising from the trunk and usually dividing.
Any of the parts of something that divides like the branch of a tree.
To arise from the trunk or a larger branch of a tree.
To produce branches.

branch.ety:
From Middle English branche, braunche, bronche, from Old French branche, branke, from Late Latin branca (“footprint”, later also “paw, claw”) (whence Middle High German pranke, German Pranke (“paw”)), of unknown origin.
Perhaps of Celtic origin, from a hypothetical Gaulish *vranca, from Proto-Indo-European *wrónk-eh₂. If so, then Indo-European cognates include Old Norse rá, vró (“angle, corner”), and possibly Lithuanian rankà (“hand”), Old Church Slavonic рѫка (rǫka, “hand”), Albanian rangë (“yardwork”).
The verb is from Middle English braunchen, from the noun.

ex.en: The large chain store created a new branch.
ex.ja: その大チェーンストアは新しく支店を作った。

ex.en: Will you take this document to the branch?
ex.ja: この書類を支社に届けてくれませんか。

ex.en: He cut off a branch from the tree.
ex.ja: 彼は木から枝を切り離した。

note.ja: ラテン語 branca（足・爪）から古フランス語を経た語。「枝」→「支店・部門」。

en: The hard, brown wood of a certain species of the tribe Caesalpinieae; originally sappan (Biancaea sappan), of the East Indies, and later …
A Brazil nut.

ex.en: Brazil supplies us with much of our coffee.
ex.ja: ブラジルはわが国のコーヒーの多くを供給している。

ex.en: I wonder what language they speak in Brazil.
ex.ja: ブラジルではどんな言葉を使うのだろう？

ex.en: In 1958, Brazil won its first World Cup victory.
ex.ja: ブラジルは1958年にワールドカップ初勝利を果たした。

note.ja: ポルトガル語 pau-brasil（赤い染料の木）から。brasa（燃えさし）。その木が多く採れる土地 →「ブラジル」。

en: The act or method of controlling or directing.
Skillful guidance or management.
To lead; to direct; to be in charge of (people or tasks)
To behave.

conduct.ety: From Late Latin conductus (“defense, escort”), from Latin conductus, perfect passive participle of condūcō (“bring together”); see also conduce. Displaced native Old English þēaw. Doublet of conduit.

ex.en: Such conduct doesn't fit in with your reputation.
ex.ja: そのような行動は、あんたの評判とは一致していない。

ex.en: A guide conducted the visitors round the museum.
ex.ja: ガイドは観光客に博物館の案内をした。

ex.en: We ask you to account for your conduct.
ex.ja: あなたの行為の責任をもってもらおう。

note.ja: con（共に）+ duct（導く）。一緒に導く →「行う・指揮する・行い」。

en: A group, set, or series of ten , particularly
A period of ten years , particularly such a period beginning with a year ending in 0 and ending with a year ending in 9.

decade.ety: From Middle English decade, from Old French decade, from Late Latin decādem (“(set of) ten”), from Ancient Greek δεκάς (dekás), from δέκα (déka, “ten”). In reference to a span of ten years, originally a clipping of the phrase decade of years. By surface analysis, dec- + -ade. Doublet of decad and dekad.

ex.en: This tree has been standing for five decades.
ex.ja: この木は５０年間ここに立っている。

ex.en: I lost my son about a decade ago.
ex.ja: 私は息子を約十年前に亡くした。

ex.en: We have experienced many changes over the last decade.
ex.ja: 過去十年間に多くの変化を経験してきた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 dekas（10のまとまり）から。deka（10）。「10年間」。decimal と同系。

en: To set apart for a deity or for religious purposes; consecrate.
To set apart for a special use.
One who dedicates themselves, or who is dedicated, to the service of some leader, religion, etc.

dedicate.ety: From Middle English dedicaten (“to dedicate”), from dedicat(e) (“dedicated”, also used as the past participle of dedicaten) + -en (verb-forming suffix), from Latin dēdicātus, the perfect passive participle of dēdicō (“to dedicate, proclaim”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix).

ex.en: The author dedicated the book to his sister.
ex.ja: 著者はその本を姉にささげた。

ex.en: His brother dedicated his life to the activity.
ex.ja: 彼の兄はその活動に命を捧げた。

ex.en: He dedicated his life to helping the poor.
ex.ja: 彼は生涯を貧しい人々を救う事に捧げた。

note.ja: ラテン語 dedicare ＝ de + dicare（宣言する）。「（神に）ささげると宣言する」→「ささげる」。dictate と同系。

en: A statement of the meaning of a word, word group, sign, or symbol; especially, a dictionary definition.
A clear instance conforming to the dictionary or textbook definition.

definition.ety: From Middle English diffinicioun, from Middle French definition, from Latin dēfīnītiō, from dēfīniō. Equivalent to define + -ition.

ex.en: Look up the definition of 'guy' in your dictionary.
ex.ja: 君の辞書で‘ｇｕｙ’の語義を調べなさい。

ex.en: Can you give me the definition of a cone?
ex.ja: 円錐形の定義を教えてくれませんか。

ex.en: What is the definition of lifestyle disease?
ex.ja: 生活習慣病の定義は何ですか？

note.ja: define（定義する）+ -ition。de + finis（境界）。「境界をはっきりさせること」→「定義・鮮明さ」。

en: A kind or helpful deed; an instance of voluntarily assisting (someone).
Goodwill; benevolent regard.
To look upon fondly; to prefer.
To use more often.

ex.ja: お願いしたい事があるのですが。

note.ja: ラテン語 favor（好意）から。favere（好意を示す）。「好意・親切な行為・支持」。favorite と同じ。

en: A piece of cloth, often decorated with an emblem, used as a visual signal or symbol.
The design that could be placed on a flag, typically a rectangular graphic that is used to represent an entity (like a country, organisat…
To furnish or deck out with flags.
To mark with a flag, especially to indicate the importance of something.

flag.ety:
From Middle English flag, flagge (“flag”), further etymology uncertain. Perhaps from or related to early Middle English flage (name for a baby's garment) and Old English flagg, flacg (“cataplasm, poultice, plaster”). Or, perhaps ultimately imitative, or otherwise drawn from Proto-Germanic *flaką (“something flat”), from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat, broad, plain”), referring to the shape.
Germanic cognates include Saterland Frisian Flaage (“flag”), West Frisian flagge (“flag”), Dutch vlag (“flag”), German Flagge (“flag”), Swedish flagga (“flag”), Danish flag (“flag, ship's flag”). Compar

ex.ja: フランスの国旗は青、白、赤です。

ex.en: The ship was flying the American flag.
ex.ja: その船はアメリカ国旗を掲げていた。

ex.en: Every country has its national flag.
ex.ja: どの国にも国旗がある。

note.ja: 16世紀からの語。語源ははっきりしない。「旗」→ 目印の「フラグ」。

en: To fit, as for a specific end or purpose; make suitable or comfortable; adapt; adjust.
To construct by fitting together or uniting various parts; fabricate by union of constituent parts.
The structural elements of a building or other constructed object.
Anything composed of parts fitted and united together; a fabric; a structure.

frame.ety:
From Middle English framen, fremen, fremmen (“to construct, build, strengthen, refresh, perform, execute, profit, avail”), from Old English framian, fremian, fremman (“to profit, avail, advance”), from Proto-West Germanic *frammjan, from Proto-Germanic *framjaną (“to further, promote, perform”), from Proto-Indo-European *promo- (“front, forward”).
Cognate with Low German framen (“to commit, effect”), Danish fremme (“to promote, further, perform”), Swedish främja (“to promote, encourage, foster”), Icelandic fremja (“to commit”). More at from.

ex.en: The frame of the building is now complete.
ex.ja: その建物の骨組みは今や完成している。

ex.en: This is a picture frame made of plastic.
ex.ja: これはプラスチック製の額縁です。

ex.en: This frame shows the painting to good advantage.
ex.ja: この額に入れると絵が引き立ちます。

note.ja: 古英語 framian（役に立つ・進める）から。「組み立てる」→「枠・骨組み」→ 罪を「でっち上げる」。

en: A recipient of hospitality, especially someone staying by invitation at the house of another.
A patron or customer in a hotel etc.
To appear as a guest, especially on a broadcast.
As a musician: to play as a guest, providing an instrument that a band/orchestra does not normally have in its line up (for instance, per…

guest.ety:
From Middle English gest, from Old Norse gestr, which replaced or was merged with Old English ġiest, both from Proto-Germanic *gastiz, from Proto-Indo-European *gʰóstis (“stranger, guest, host, someone with whom one has reciprocal duties of hospitality”). Doublet of host, from Latin.

ex.en: There are five other guests at the hotel.
ex.ja: ホテルには、他に５人の客がいます。

ex.en: There were plenty of guests in the hall.
ex.ja: ホールにはたくさんの客がいた。

ex.en: It's almost time for the guest to arrive.
ex.ja: そろそろお客が来る時間だ。

note.ja: 古北欧語 gestr から。ラテン語 hostis（よそ者・敵）、host と同じ祖先。

en: The abode of God and of the angels and saints in His presence.
The abode of the Abrahamic God; similar abodes of the gods in other religions and traditions, such as Mount Olympus.

heaven.ety:
From a wide variety of Middle English forms including hevene, heven, hevin, and hewin (“heaven, sky”), from Old English heofon, heofone (“heaven, sky”), from Proto-West Germanic *hebn (“heaven, sky”), of uncertain origin.
Cognate with Scots heiven, hewin (“heaven, sky”), Middle Dutch heven (“sky, heaven”), Low German Heven (“heaven, sky”), and possibly the rare Icelandic and Old Norse hifinn (“heaven, sky”), which are all probably dissimilated forms of the Germanic root which appears in Old Norse himinn (“heaven, sky”), Gothic 𐌷𐌹𐌼𐌹𐌽𐍃 (himins, “heaven, sky”), Old Swedish himin, Old Danish himæn

ex.en: For the love of Heaven, don't get angry.
ex.ja: お願いだから、怒らないでください。

ex.en: God created the heaven and the earth.
ex.ja: 神は天と地を創造した。

ex.en: I can wait to love in heaven.
ex.ja: 天国で愛しあえるまで待ってるよ。

note.ja: 古英語 heofon から。「空」→「天国」。

en: The quality or state of being independent; lack of dependence; the state of not being reliant on, or controlled by, others.
The state of having sufficient means for a comfortable livelihood.

ex.en: He said that America declared its independence in 1776.
ex.ja: アメリカは１７７６年に独立を宣言したと彼は言った。

ex.en: The people of America fought for their independence.
ex.ja: 米国の人民は独立のために戦った。

ex.en: India gained independence from Britain in 1947.
ex.ja: インドは英国から１９４７年に独立した。

note.ja: in（否定）+ de（下に）+ pend（ぶら下がる）+ ence。何にもぶら下がっていないこと →「独立」。

en: A long-established organization or type of organization, particularly one involved with education, public service, or charity work.
A custom or practice of a society or community.

institution.ety: From Middle English institucioun, from Old French institution, from Latin institūtiō, from instituō (“to set up”), from in- (“in, on”) + statuō (“to set up, establish”). Equivalent to institute + -ion.

ex.en: The institution was established in the late 1960s.
ex.ja: その機関は１９６０年代後半に設立された。

ex.en: This institution came into being after the war.
ex.ja: この組織は戦後生まれた。

ex.en: Writing new year's cards is a Japanese institution.
ex.ja: 年賀状を書くのは日本の習慣である。

note.ja: in（中に）+ stit（立てる）+ ution。中に打ち立てたもの →「機関・制度・施設」。

en: To touch with the lips or press the lips against, usually to show love or affection or passion, or as part of a greeting.
To (cause to) touch lightly or slightly; to come into contact.
A touch with the lips, usually to express love or affection, or as a greeting.
An 'X' mark placed at the end of a letter or other type of message, signifying the bestowal of a kiss from the sender to the receiver.

kiss.ety:
From Middle English kissen, kussen, from Old English cyssan (“to kiss”), from Proto-West Germanic *kussijan, from Proto-Germanic *kussijaną (“to kiss”).
Cognates include Saterland Frisian küsje, Dutch kussen, German Low German küssen, German küssen, Danish and Norwegian Bokmål kysse, Faroese, Icelandic, Norwegian Nynorsk, and Swedish kyssa. Compare Proto-Indo-European *ku-, *kus- (probably imitative), with descendants including Ancient Greek κύσσω (kússō), poetic form of κύσω (kúsō, “to kiss”), and Hittite [script needed] (kuwassanzi, “they kiss”).

ex.en: Tom was hoping that Mary would kiss him.
ex.ja: トムは、メアリーがキスすることを望んでいました。

ex.en: How did you know Tom would kiss Mary?
ex.ja: どうしてトムがメアリーにキスするって分かったの？

ex.en: Tom gave Mary a kiss on the lips.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーの唇にキスをした。

note.ja: 古英語 cyssan から。擬音的な語とされる。

en: A burden; a weight to be carried.
A worry or concern to be endured, especially in the phrase a load off one's mind.
To put a load on or in (a means of conveyance or a place of storage).
To place in or on a conveyance or a place of storage.

load.ety:
The sense of “burden” first arose in the 13th century as a secondary meaning of Middle English lode, loade, which had the main significance of “way, course, journey”, from Old English lād (“course, journey; way, street, waterway; leading, carrying; maintenance, support”) (ultimately from Proto-Germanic *laidō (“leading, way”), Proto-Indo-European *leyt- (“to go, go forth, die”).

ex.en: The news was a load off his mind.
ex.ja: その知らせを聞いて彼の重荷が取れた。

ex.en: This car can carry a load of 4 tons.
ex.ja: この車は４トン車だ。

ex.en: His success took a load off my mind.
ex.ja: 彼の成功で私の心の重荷がおりた。

note.ja: 古英語 lād（道・運ぶこと）から。lead（導く）と同系。「積み荷」→「負担」→ データを「読み込む」。

en: The course of a story, comprising a series of incidents which are gradually unfolded, sometimes by unexpected means.
An area or land used for building on or planting on.
To conceive (a crime, misdeed etc).
To trace out (a graph or diagram).

plot.ety:
From Middle English plot, plotte, from late Old English plot (“a plot of ground”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Proto-Germanic *plataz, *platjaz (“a patch”); or alternatively, perhaps from a rebracketing of Old English land-splott (“small portion, or plot, of ground”) taken as landes-plot (“plot of land”). Compare Middle Low German plet (“patch, strip of cloth, rags”), German Bletz (“rags, bits, strip of land”), and possibly Gothic 𐍀𐌻𐌰𐍄 (plat, “a patch, rags”). See also plat. See also complot for an influence and reinforcement of noun sense 8.
Noun sense 12 is a back-formation from for th

ex.en: Apart from the plot, the book interested me.
ex.ja: 筋書きは別として、その本は私をひきつけた。

ex.en: I saw through their plot at once.
ex.ja: 私は彼らの陰謀をすぐに見抜いた。

en: Of or pertaining to competition.

competitive.ety: From Latin competītus (past participle of competere) + -ive.

ex.en: Japan is highly competitive in high technology industries.
ex.ja: 日本はハイテク産業の競争力がある。

ex.en: To many people today, "competitive" is a bad word.
ex.ja: 現在、「競争」を悪い言葉と思っている人は多い。

ex.en: Tom and Mary are both really competitive.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーは二人ともとても競争的だ。

note.ja: compete（競う）+ -itive。com + petere（求める）。「共に求める」→「競争の」。

en: The food and beverage a person or animal consumes.
A controlled regimen of food and drink choices, as to gain or lose weight or otherwise influence health.
Containing less fat, salt, sugar, or calories than normal, or claimed to have such.
Having certain traits subtracted.
To modify one's food and beverage intake so as to decrease or increase body weight or influence health.

diet.ety: From Middle English diet, dyet, diete, from Old French diete, from Medieval Latin dieta (“regimen, regulation; assembly”), from Latin diaeta, from Ancient Greek δίαιτα (díaita).

ex.en: I think you'd better go on a diet.
ex.ja: 君は食事を減らした方がいいと思う。

ex.en: She is on a diet to lose weight.
ex.ja: 彼女はやせるためにダイエットをしています。

ex.en: I believe more in diet than in drugs.
ex.ja: 薬より食餌療法の方が効くと信じています。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 diaita（生活様式）から。「食生活」→「ダイエット」。「国会」は中世ラテン語 dieta（会議の日）からで別語（dies：日）。

en: A product of fertilization in a plant, specifically
The seed-bearing part of a plant; often edible, colourful, fragrant, and sweet or sour; produced from a floral ovary after fertilization.
To produce fruit, seeds, or spores.

ex.ja: どんな種類の果物が一番好きですか。

ex.en: Present supplies of fruit are short of requirements.
ex.ja: 現在における果物の供給は需要に及ばない。

note.ja: ラテン語 fructus（楽しみ・収穫）から。frui（楽しむ）。「収穫物」→「果物・成果」。

en: An alphabetical listing of items and their location.
The index finger; the forefinger.
To arrange an index for something, especially a long text.
To inventory; to take stock.

ex.ja: 株価指数は昨日200ポイント下げた。

ex.en: The price index hit an all-time high.
ex.ja: 物価指数はこれまでの最高に達した。

ex.en: It is an index of her character.
ex.ja: それは彼女の性格の表れだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 index（人差し指・指し示すもの）から。indicare（指し示す）。「索引・指数」。index finger は人差し指。

en: A road, street, or similar thoroughfare.
A narrow passageway between fences, walls, hedges or trees.

lane.ety:
From Middle English lane, lone, from Old English lanu (“a lane, alley, avenue”), from Proto-West Germanic *lanu, from Proto-Germanic *lanō (“lane, passageway”).
Cognate with Scots lone (“cattle-track, by-road”), West Frisian leane, loane (“a walkway, avenue”), Dutch laan (“alley, avenue”), German Low German Lane, Laan (“lane”), Swedish lån (“covered walkway encircling a house”), Icelandic lön (“a row of houses”).

ex.en: In Japan, almost all roads are single-lane.
ex.ja: 日本ではほとんど全ての道路は単車線だ。

ex.en: Leaves lay thick in the lane.
ex.ja: 小道に落ち葉が厚く積もっていた。

ex.en: A bulldozer was used to level the lane.
ex.ja: その土地をならすのにブルドーザーが使われた。

note.ja: 古英語 lanu から。「小道」→「車線」。

en: A thing or group of things in a disagreeable, disorganised, or dirty state; hence a bad situation.
A large quantity or number.
To make soiled by defecating.
To make soiled by ejaculating.

mess.ety: Perhaps a corruption of Middle English mesh (“mash”), compare muss, or derived from Etymology 2 "mixed foods, as for animals". Compare also Old English mes (“dung, excrement”).

ex.en: Who's going to clear up all this mess?
ex.ja: 誰がこの混乱のあとかたづけをすることになっているか。

ex.en: Who's responsible for this mess in the kitchen?
ex.ja: 台所をこんなに散らかしたのは誰だよ。

ex.en: My brother leaves his room in a mess.
ex.ja: 弟は部屋をちらかしっぱなしにしている。

note.ja: 古フランス語 mes（食事の一皿）から。ラテン語 missus（置かれた）。ごちゃ混ぜの食べ物 →「散らかった状態」。軍隊の「食堂」の意味も残る。

en: A country's entire maritime military force, including ships and personnel.
A governmental department in charge of a country's maritime military force.
Having the dark blue colour of navy blue.
Belonging to the navy; typical of the navy.

navy.ety:
From Middle English nave, navye, from Anglo-Norman, Old French navie, from Latin nāvigia < nāvigium, from Latin nāvigō, nāvis (“boat”), from Proto-Indo-European *néh₂us. Compare Ancient Greek ναῦς (naûs, “ship”), Persian ناو (nâv, “boat, warship”), Sanskrit नाव (nāva, “ship”), Old English nōwend (“mariner, sailor”). By surface analysis, Latin nav- + -y.
Displaced native Old English sċiphere (literally “ship army”).

ex.en: Mary was wearing a navy blue dress.
ex.ja: メアリーは紺色のドレスを身にまとっていた。

ex.en: My father was in the navy.
ex.ja: 父は海軍にいた。

ex.en: I'm looking for a navy blue raincoat, size 36.
ex.ja: ネービーブルーのレインコートを探しているんですよ、サイズは３６なんだけど。

note.ja: ラテン語 navis（船）から。船の集まり →「海軍・紺色（ネイビーブルー）」。navigate（航海する）も同じ。

ex.en: I normally don't do things like this.
ex.ja: 普段はこういうことはしないよ。

ex.en: Which search engine do you normally use?
ex.ja: 検索エンジンって、普段何使ってる？

note.ja: ラテン語 norma（定規）から。基準どおりに →「普通は・正常に」。

en: To happen or take place.
To present or offer itself.

occur.ety: Originally "meet (in argument)", borrowed from Middle French occurrer, from Latin occurrō (“run to meet, run against, befall, present itself”) from prefix ob- (“against”) + verb currō (“run, hurry, move”).

ex.en: What would you do if another war occurred?
ex.ja: また戦争が起こったら、あなたはどうしますか。

ex.en: Just then, a bright idea occurred to me.
ex.ja: ちょうどその時、うまい考えが浮かんだ。

ex.en: It was an event that occurred only rarely.
ex.ja: それはまれにしか起こらない事件だった。

note.ja: oc（〜に向かって）+ cur（走る）。〜に走り出てくる →「起こる・（考えが）浮かぶ」。

en: The action of opposing or of being in conflict.
An opposite or contrasting position.

opposition.ety: From Middle English opposicioun, from Old French oposicion (whence French opposition), from Late Latin oppositiō, translating Ancient Greek ἀντίθεσις (antíthesis), from the past participle stem of classical Latin oppōnō (“to set against”). Equivalent to oppose + -ition.

ex.en: The community scheme has run up against local opposition.
ex.ja: 地域計画は住民の反対に直面している。

ex.en: He has no basis for his opposition.
ex.ja: 彼に反対する根拠がない。

ex.en: He couldn't help doing so in the face of opposition.
ex.ja: 反対に直面してそうせざるを得なかった。

note.ja: op（逆らって）+ pos（置く）+ ition。反対側に置くこと →「反対・対立・野党」。

en: Without end, eternal.
Lasting for an indefinitely long time.
A chemical hair treatment imparting or removing curliness, whose effects typically last for a period of weeks; a perm.
Given an n×n matrix a_ij,, the sum over all permutations π, of ∏ᵢ₌₁ⁿa_iπ(i).

permanent.ety: From Middle English permanent, permanente, from Middle French permanent, from Latin permanēns, from permaneō (“to stay through”). First attested in the 15th century.

ex.en: Do you want your permanent to look natural?
ex.ja: パーマは自然な感じにしますか。

ex.en: We all wish for permanent world peace.
ex.ja: 私たちみんな恒久的な世界平和を願っています。

ex.en: My daughter is cutting her permanent teeth.
ex.ja: 娘の永久歯がはえてきました。

note.ja: ラテン語 permanere ＝ per（通して）+ manere（とどまる）。「ずっととどまる」→「永久的な」。remain と同じ man。

en: In a personal manner.
In person.

personally.ety: From Middle English personally, personely, personallich, personaliche, equivalent to personal + -ly.

ex.en: Well, personally, I don't really care for it.
ex.ja: そうですね、私としては、あまり好みません。

ex.en: The president conducted us personally to his office.
ex.ja: 大統領自ら我々を執務室に案内してくれた。

ex.en: Personally, I find French more difficult than English.
ex.ja: 私的には、フランス語の方が英語より難しい。

note.ja: personal（個人の）+ -ly。「個人的には・自分で」。

en: A state of being pleased or contented; gratification.
A person, thing or action that causes enjoyment.
pleased to meet you, "It's my pleasure"
To give or afford pleasure to.
To give sexual pleasure to.

pleasure.ety: From Early Modern English pleasur, plesur, alteration (with ending accommodated to -ure) of Middle English plaisir (“pleasure”), from Old French plesir, plaisir (“to please”), infinitive used as a noun, conjugated form of plaisir or plaire, from Latin placeō (“to please, to seem good”), from the Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂-k- (“wide and flat”). Related to Dutch plezier (“pleasure, fun”). More at please.

ex.en: To see you is always a great pleasure.
ex.ja: 君に会うのはいつだってうれしいことです。

ex.en: It is a great pleasure being with you.
ex.ja: 君と一緒にいるのはとても楽しい。

ex.en: Swimming in the ocean is my greatest pleasure.
ex.ja: 海で泳ぐことは私の一番の楽しみだ。

note.ja: please（喜ばせる）+ -ure。「喜び」。

en: To be in the habit of choosing something rather than something else; to favor; to like better.
To present or submit (something) to an authority (now usually in "to prefer charges").

prefer.ety: From Middle English preferren, from Anglo-Norman preferer, from Latin praeferō. Displaced native Old English foresettan and foreberan. Doublet of prelate. See also infer, relate and refer, delate and defer, as well as collate and confer among others.

ex.en: I prefer going out to staying at home.
ex.ja: 私は家にいるよりも外出するほうがいい。

ex.en: I prefer the former plan to the latter.
ex.ja: はじめの計画のほうが後のより良いと思う。

ex.en: Of soccer and rugby, I prefer the latter.
ex.ja: サッカーとラグビーでは後者の方が好きだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 praeferre ＝ prae（前に）+ ferre（運ぶ）。「前に置く」→「〜のほうを好む」。transfer と同じ fer。

en: Typical; having the same properties or interest as a larger group.
Representing, showing a likeness.
Someone who represents others as a member of a legislative or governing body.
One who speaks for or acts on behalf of another in a particular (especially official) capacity.

representative.ety: From Middle English representative, from Middle French representatif and its etymon Medieval Latin repraesentātīvus. By surface analysis, represent + -ative; See representation. Displaced native Old English spala (“a representative”).

ex.en: All the students recognized her as their representative.
ex.ja: 学生全員が彼女を自分達の代表と認めた。

ex.en: Our representative argued against the new tax plan.
ex.ja: 我々の代表は新税の計画に異論を唱えた。

ex.en: He attended the meeting as our company representative.
ex.ja: 彼はわが社の代表として会議に参加しました。

note.ja: represent（代表する）+ -ative。re + praesentare（差し出す）。「代表者」→（米）「下院議員」。

en: A representation of the aspects of the celestial bodies for any moment or at a given event.
A systematic plan of future action.
To plot, or contrive a plan; to maneuver.
To plan; to contrive; to maneuver.

scheme.ety: From late Middle English scheame, from Medieval Latin schēma (“figure, form”), from Ancient Greek σχῆμα (skhêma, “form, shape”), from ἔχω (ékhō, “to hold”). Doublet of schema. Compare sketch.

ex.en: There is a scheme to expand the company.
ex.ja: その会社では拡張の計画があります。

ex.en: They were at the bottom of the scheme.
ex.ja: 彼らがその陰謀の黒幕であった。

ex.en: She denied having taken part in the scheme.
ex.ja: 彼女はそのたくらみに加わったことを否定した。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 skhēma（形・図）から。「図式」→「計画」→「たくらみ」。schema と同じ。

en: A movement to do something, a beginning.
An act of shifting; a slight movement or change.
To move from one place to another; to redistribute.
To change in form or character; switch.

ex.en: Starting next week, I'll be on the late shift.
ex.ja: 来週から遅番勤務になったよ。

ex.en: Starting next week, I'll be working the late shift.
ex.ja: 来週から遅番勤務になったよ。

An open container or pool for storing water or other liquids.
To fail or fall (often used in describing the economy or the stock market); to degenerate or decline rapidly; to plummet.
To attract the attacks of an enemy target in cooperative team-based combat, so that one's teammates can defeat the enemy in question more…

en: To make a tender of; to offer or tender.
To be likely, or probable to do something, or to have a certain habit or leaning.

tend.ety: From Middle English tenden, from Middle French tendre, from Old French tendre (“to stretch, stretch out, hold forth, offer, tender”), from Latin tendere (“to stretch, stretch out, extend, spread out”).

ex.en: People who ignore history tend to repeat it.
ex.ja: 歴史を無視する人はとかくあやまちを繰り返しがちだ。

ex.en: Women tend to live longer than men.
ex.ja: 女性は男性より長生きする傾向がある。

ex.en: Japanese people tend to think that way.
ex.ja: 日本人はそのように考える傾向がある。

en: Firmly held together; compact; not loose or open.
Unyielding or firm.
Firmly, so as not to come loose easily.
Soundly.

In contrast with; as opposed to.

To dislike.
To cancel a "like" action.

unlike.ety: From Middle English unlic, unlich, from Old English unlīċ, unġelīċ (“unlike, different, dissimilar, diverse”), from Proto-Germanic *ungalīkaz. By surface analysis, un- + like. Cognate with Dutch ongelijk, German ungleich, Old Norse úlíkr (see there for North Germanic descendants).

ex.en: The two brothers are quite unlike in their appearance.
ex.ja: その二人の兄弟は風采がまったく違う。

ex.en: It's unlike him to get so angry.
ex.ja: あんなに怒るなんて彼らしくない。

ex.en: It is unlike him to be late.
ex.ja: 遅刻するなんて彼らしくない。

note.ja: un（否定）+ like（似ている）。「〜と違って」。

en: Once every week.
Every week.
Of or relating to a week.
Happening once a week, or every week.
A publication that is published once a week.

weekly.ety: From Middle English wykely (adverb), equivalent to week + -ly (adverbial suffix) or week + -ly (adjectival suffix). Compare Dutch wekelijks (“weekly”), German wöchentlich (“weekly”), Danish ugentlig (“weekly”), Norwegian ukentlig (“weekly”), Icelandic vikulega (“weekly”), Swedish veckovis (“weekly”).

ex.en: Tom bought a weekly magazine at the station.
ex.ja: トムは駅で週刊誌を買った。

ex.en: The boy sat there reading a weekly magazine.
ex.ja: 少年はそこに座って週刊誌を読んでいた。

ex.en: This weekly comes out once a week.
ex.ja: この週刊誌は毎週１回発行される。

note.ja: week（週）+ -ly。「毎週の」。

en: A small, usually uncultivated area adjoining or (now especially) within the precincts of a house or other building.
The property surrounding one's house, typically dominated by one's lawn.
To confine to a yard.

ex.ja: 日本では広い庭はなかなかありません。

ex.en: He let the dog loose in the yard.
ex.ja: 彼は犬を庭に放した。

en: Any one out of an indefinite number of persons; anyone; any person.
A person of some consideration or standing.

anybody.ety: From Middle English ani-bodi, anybodi, eny body. By surface analysis, any + body.

ex.en: I don't know anybody here in this town.
ex.ja: この町には知り合いはいません。

ex.en: I can't get this work done by anybody.
ex.ja: この仕事は誰にもしてもらうわけにはいかない。

ex.en: Whatever happens, I'll not tell anybody about it.
ex.ja: 口が裂けてもそのことは口外しません。

note.ja: any + body（人）。「誰か・誰でも」。

Any item recorded on the left-hand side of a balance sheet.

ex.ja: 資産にはどんなものが含まれるのでしょうか。

ex.ja: この建物は国の文化財です。

en: A sport in which two opposing teams of five players strive to put a ball through a hoop.
The particular kind of ball used in the sport of basketball.
To play basketball.
To throw in a similar way to when shooting a basketball.

en: A knob or disc that is passed through a loop or (buttonhole), serving as a fastener.
A mechanical device designed to be pressed with a finger in order to open or close an electric circuit or to activate a mechanism.
To fasten with a button.
To be fastened by a button or buttons.

button.ety: From Middle English boton, botoun, from Old French boton (Modern French bouton), from Old French bouter, boter (“to push; thrust”), ultimately from a Germanic language. Doublet of bouton, Biden, and beat. More at butt.

ex.en: The button on your coat is coming off.
ex.ja: 君の上着のボタンがとれかかっているよ。

ex.en: In case of an emergency, push this button.
ex.ja: 緊急の場合は、このボタンを押しなさい。

ex.en: Press the red button if something strange happens.
ex.ja: 何かおかしなことが起こったら赤いボタンを押しなさい。

note.ja: 古フランス語 boton（つぼみ・突起）から。bouter（押す）。押す「ボタン」。butt と同系。

en: A battle, a fight (often one in which weapons are used).
a struggle for victory
To fight; to struggle against.
To fight (with); to struggle for victory (against).

ex.en: The city is working hard to combat crime.
ex.ja: 市は犯罪に対抗するために懸命に取り組んでいる。

note.ja: フランス語 combattre ＝ com + battre（打つ）。「打ち合う」→「戦闘」。battle、debate と同じ。

en: The act, or process of setting something up, or establishing something; the composition or structure of such a thing; its makeup.

ex.en: The wet climate did not agree with his constitution.
ex.ja: 湿気の多い気候が彼の体質に合わなかった。

note.ja: con（共に）+ stit（立てる）+ ution。共に打ち立てたもの →「構成・体格・憲法」。

ex.ja: チケットはカウンターでお受けとりください。

ex.ja: カウンターではテニスシューズを販売している。

en: Something created such as an invention or artwork.
The act of creating something.

creation.ety: Inherited from Middle English creacion, from Old French creacion (modern French création), from Latin creātiō, creātiōnis. By surface analysis, create + -ion. Displaced native Old English ġesċeaft.

ex.en: Man is the lord of all creation.
ex.ja: 人間は万物の霊長である。

ex.en: Rock and roll was a creation of the young generation.
ex.ja: ロックンロールは若い世代の発明だった。

ex.en: Since I recovered from my serious illness, all of creation is beautiful to me.
ex.ja: 大病からようやく生還した私の目には、森羅万象が美しく映った。

note.ja: create（創造する）+ -ion。ラテン語 creare。「創造・作品」。

en: A royal, imperial or princely headdress; a diadem.
A wreath or band for the head, especially one given as reward of victory or a mark of honor.
Of, related to, or pertaining to a crown.
Of, related to, pertaining to the top of a tree or trees.
To place a crown on the head of.
To formally declare (someone) a king, queen, emperor, etc.

crown.ety:
Inherited from Middle English coroune, from Anglo-Norman corone, from Latin corōna (“crown, wreath”), from Ancient Greek κορώνη (korṓnē). Doublet of corona, korona, koruna, krona, króna, and krone. Displaced Old English corenbēag (“crown”) and Middle English kinehelm, kynehelm, from Old English cynehelm (“crown”, literally “kinhelm” or “king's helm”).
The paper sizes (etymology 1, noun sense 18) are so called because the papers were originally watermarked with a crown.

ex.en: You have to have a new crown.
ex.ja: 新しいクラウンをかぶせる必要があります。

ex.en: He has never been crowned with such glory.
ex.ja: 彼はかつてそのような栄光を与えられたことはなかった。

ex.en: I've lost my crown.
ex.ja: クラウンが取れました。

note.ja: ラテン語 corona（冠）から。「王冠」→「王位」。corolla と同じ。

en: To determine with precision; to mark out with distinctness; to ascertain or exhibit clearly.
To express the essential nature of something.
A kind of macro in source code that replaces one text string with another wherever it occurs.

define.ety: From Middle English definen, from Old French definer, variant of definir, from Latin dēfīniō (“limit, settle, define”), from dē + fīniō (“set a limit, bound, end”).

ex.en: The tree was clearly defined against the sky.
ex.ja: その木は空にくっきりと浮かび上がっていた。

ex.en: Physics can be defined as the science of matter, motion, and energy.
ex.ja: 物理学は物質、運動、エネルギーの科学であると定義することができる。

ex.en: Can you clearly define this word?
ex.ja: この語を明確に定義できますか。

note.ja: ラテン語 definire ＝ de + finis（境界）。「境界を決める」→「定義する」。finish と同じ fin。
